options.label: Appears to be fraud, but is not
options.description: False positive / apparent fraud with an innocent explanation.

options.label: Petty fraud
options.description: The example given was minor expense misuse.

options.label: Large-scale financial misstatement
options.description: Preserve this approved label within the fraud family; intent still has to be specified in the authored case.

options.label: Collusion between internal employees and vendors
options.description: Coordinated conduct spanning company and vendor participants.

options.label: Fraud discovered by an external whistleblower
options.description: Preserve the external-whistleblower discovery route, not merely a generic anomaly.

options.label: Missing key documents entirely
options.description: The requested document is not supplied at all.

options.label: Over-redacted documents

options.label: Screenshots of system references without actual documents
options.description: The owner described receiving a screenshot of an internal SharePoint reference showing that an audit committee charter exists, rather than the charter itself.

options.label: Draft versions instead of final versions
options.description: The requested final or signed version is replaced by a draft.

options.label: Out-of-scope substitutes

options.label: Summaries or descriptions instead of source evidence
options.description: An explanation or summary is provided instead of the underlying support.

options.label: Obsolete versions
options.description: An outdated policy, report, or other version is supplied.

options.description: The source or authorship of the supplied evidence cannot be established from what was provided.

options.label: Incomplete approval chains
options.description: Only some required signoffs or approval steps are visible.

options.label: Unreadable formats
options.description: Proprietary, corrupted, or otherwise unreadable files prevent inspection.

options.label: Demonstrated but not evidenced
options.description: The owner described a genuine live process whose connected MFA/VPN/application path is difficult to capture and document. The intended problem is the support or linkage available to the auditor, not necessarily failure of the underlying process.

options.label: Misinterpretation of evidence requests

options.description: Responses are delayed because the team is unsure how to respond.

options.label: Over-reliance on higher-ups
options.description: The team escalates routine decisions to senior personnel.

options.label: Poor documentation of their own processes
options.description: The team lacks usable documentation explaining its processes.

options.label: Difficulty explaining controls
options.description: Walkthrough explanations are confused or incomplete.

options.label: Redaction and over-redaction
options.description: The owner explicitly added this sixth symptom.

options.label: New business line added mid-audit

options.label: Previously excluded geographic locations included

options.label: New regulatory framework required

options.label: Previously scoped-out IT systems brought into scope
options.description: Additional systems become relevant to the work.

options.label: Client internal control framework changes

options.description: Preserve the agreed event; the earlier statement assigning audit materiality to the client was subsequently identified as incorrect by the research comparison.

options.label: Management reviews every evidence item before release

options.description: The discussed scenario bypasses the client’s normal evidence-control route.

options.label: Management changes audit evidence after feedback
options.description: Preserve this label; whether a change is a legitimate correction, filtering, or misconduct must be specified in the actual case.

options.label: Audit committee requests additional procedures
options.description: Additional work is requested outside the original scope.

options.label: Management pre-screens questions and delays meetings
